abstract: The comprehensive specification of palaeo-diets has depended upon the preservation of plants and bones in archaeological deposits, which is limited by preservation conditions. Although middens at settlement sites in northern Norway can have comprehensive faunal archives they still may not reflect the full diet. Here, we apply sedaDNA metabarcoding and shotgun sequencing to two midden complexes in Finnmark, Norway. At both sites, this doubled the species identified. At the Bankgohppi "Gressbakken" house site (c.4.5-3.8 BP), items were added to all food categories (Figure below) including mammals such as reindeer, beaver, and bowhead whale, suggesting deep-sea fishing practice. At the Finnes coastal Sami Early Metal Age site (c.07-0.8 BP) and later Norse Medieval re-occupation, sedaDNA added terrestrial mammal (reindeer) and domesticated stock (goat, cattle) to the diet. The combination of traditional data with sedaDNA data provides us for the first time with a broad spectrum, suggesting seasonally balanced diets and fishing activity in northern Norway over the last 4000 years.
